subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Nissan GT-R
description: A quick win: understand The Nissan GT-R.

hook.text: The Nissan GT-R embarrassed supercars costing five times more. Magazines called it 'Godzilla.'

buildup.text: Its twin-turbo V6, all-wheel drive, and launch control made it brutally fast in a straight line.

discovery.text: It hit 60 mph in under 3 seconds when it launched in 2007—matching Ferraris and Lamborghinis.

twist.text: It cost $70,000 when a comparable Ferrari cost $300,000. The value gap was embarrassing for Europeans.

climax.text: The GT-R proved that engineering discipline could beat exotic materials and badge prestige.

punchline.text: Godzilla didn't need a fancy badge to dominate.

quiz.question: Why was the GT-R called 'Godzilla'?
options: It destroyed supercars at a fraction of the cost

details.summary: The Nissan GT-R, codenamed Godzilla, is a twin-turbo all-wheel-drive supercar killer that consistently beats cars costing three times its price through advanced electronics and engineering precision.
details.whyItMatters: The GT-R proved that technology and software can rival exotic materials and brand cachet. It democratized supercar performance, embarrassing Ferraris and Porsches at a fraction of their price.
takeaways: Its twin-turbo V6 and AWD system launch from 0 to 60 in under 3 seconds
Advanced electronics manage power delivery thousands of times per second
It earned the nickname Godzilla for destroying exotic rivals on track

faq.question: How does the GT-R compete with much more expensive cars?
faq.answer: Its launch control, sophisticated all-wheel drive, and dual-clutch transmission are electronically optimized to extract maximum performance. The technology compensates for areas where exotics use costly materials.

faq.question: Is the GT-R still competitive today?
faq.answer: The current R35 generation launched in 2007 and has been continuously updated. While newer rivals have caught up, the GT-R remains remarkably fast for its price and a new generation is anticipated.
